newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end slightly higher on cash-bond buying.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end slightly higher on cash-bond buying.

text.p: Key March Japanese government bond futures ended slightly higher on Tuesday, after a sharp recovery in the afternoon due to buying of cash JGBs by an institutional investor.
A major life insurer apparently bought a large amount of cash JGBs with around seven-year maturities in the afternoon, traders said.
There was talk that the life insurer bought a total of 200 billion yen worth of cash bonds, a city bank trader said.
The March ended at 126.40, up slightly from the previous day's close of 126.30. Turnover was 37,790 contracts.
Traders said there was talk that the life insurer bought the 164th issue, and also JGBs between the 170th to the 179th issues.
In morning trade, the life insurer apparently sold 20-year JGBs, which helped to dampen market sentiment, a trader for another city bank said.
Sentiment was also weakened in morning trade due to a rise in Tokyo share prices and hedge-selling of the March ahead of the release of results of a six-year JGB auction, traders said.
But JGBs were supported on the downside in the morning as cash bonds were bought on dips, a brokerage trader said.
There was talk that a second-tier life insurer bought cash JGBs between the 190th and 193rd issues in the morning, when the March dropped to around 126.00, the trader for a brokerage house said.
The Ministry of Finance offered 500 billion yen in 1.6 percent six-year government bonds through a price-competitive auction on Tuesday.
MOF said the auction produced a lowest price of 99.30 and an average price 99.44.
Traders said there seemed to be moderate investor demand for the new six-year bonds.

"We were able to sell (to investors) all the six-year bonds we purchased through the auction," the trader for a brokerage house said. Investor appetite for under par bonds had not waned, the trader said.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.405 percent as of 0704 GMT, down from the previous day's close of 2.410 percent.

The June contract was now the new benchmark, as its turnover exceeded that of the March in Tuesday trade, traders said. The June's turnover for the day was 57,321 contracts compared to 37,790 contracts for the March.
